result:
I've fixed all four reports. Search now follows your rule when you archive or restore an issue or project and when comments or edits arrive later, and the rebuild leaves exactly the allowed entries. The full suite passes (625 tests) and `tsc` and `eslint` are clean.

- **Archiving an issue or project (reports 1 and 2):** archiving an issue now also removes its comments from the index. Archiving a project removes it and all its issues and comments, whether or not the issues were archived with it. Comments and issue edits made afterwards on kept issues stay hidden.
- **Restoring a project (report 3):** restore brings back the project plus its live issues and their live comments. Issues archived with the project, or on their own earlier, stay hidden along with their comments.
- **Rebuild (report 4):** the rebuild job now reads every page of projects, issues and comments, so large workspaces are covered. It only indexes what the rule allows, then deletes every other entry for that workspace, including ghosts, deleted comments and duplicate rows. It never touches another workspace's rows. If any item fails to index, it skips the delete step and logs a warning, so a partial run can't remove valid entries.

I made a few changes beyond the four reports:
- **New events:** I added `project.updated` and `comment.updated`, emitted from `updateProject` and `updateComment`. Edited comments and project names previously kept their old search text, and these events let the index refresh them.
- **Query-time guard:** search also hides any entry whose source row is archived or sits under an archived parent, even if the index hasn't caught up yet. Results and the reported total use the same filter.
- **Writer return value:** `indexIssue`, `indexComment` and `indexProject` now return whether the entry is in the index afterwards. Existing callers that ignore the return value are unaffected.

The main changes are in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`, `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts` and `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts`. I added `tests/services/search-lifecycle.test.ts` covering each report, including a rebuild over more than 100 issues per page.
